newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government hoping for rate cut - Veltroni.
newsitem.headline: Italian government hoping for rate cut - Veltroni.

text.p: The Italian government hopes the official discount rate will fall further, given the falling trend in inflation, but the decision is exclusively one for the Bank of Italy, deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said.

"Obviously a government which sees there is a very high differential between actual rates and inflation, hopes and expects that sooner or later there can be a further reduction in interest rates," Veltroni said at the fringe of a trades union federation conference.
But he stressed this issue was "exclusively the responsibility of the Bank of Italy."
Preliminary inflation data from four sample cities on Tuesday indicated May inflation is running at 1.5 percent year on year, down from 1.7 percent in April and March's 2.2 percent.

If confirmed by data from a further seven cities after 1530 GMT today, many in the financial markets speculate the Bank of Italy may lower the discount rate by 50 to 75 basis points if not in the next few days then by the end of the month.
The central bank last cut the discount rate by 75 basis points to 6.75 percent in January.
